page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highcpu-2 is a compute-oriented virtual machine configuration powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with multithreading enabled and dedicated CPU allocation. Memory capacity is allocated at 4.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 core-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Cache sizing includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The platform incorporates modern vector and cryptography instruction extensions, including AVX-512 (supporting VNNI and BF16), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance includes no bundled local storage and features zero GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage architectures.

Benchmark results demonstrate high single-threaded performance alongside constrained overall throughput, typical of a dual-vCPU footprint. The AMD EPYC 9B45 core attains top-tier results in single-core stress-ng tests (3437.06) and Geekbench 6 single-core execution (2493.0), as well as top-tier compression metrics (37.39 GB/sec in gzip and 16.63 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3). In contrast, total parallel compute capacity ranks in the lower quartile due to the two-thread limit, as seen in multi-core Geekbench (3185.0) and PassMark CPU evaluations (4641.74). Memory bandwidth registers in the average bracket for uncached large blocks, reaching 45.68 GB/sec read and 26.65 GB/sec write throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server balances modern Zen architecture per-core performance with a streamlined memory footprint. The allocation avoids paying for excess RAM capacity when tasks do not require large working sets, while providing dedicated execution time on an enterprise AMD processor. The absence of local NVMe storage requires careful consideration of external disk bandwidth and associated networking overhead.

The n4d-highcpu-2 instance is suitable for lightweight, single-thread-intensive workloads, task runners, build workers handling small codebases, CI/CD pipeline steps, text processing pipelines, and modest static web serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor, providing 2 vCPUs across 1 physical dedicated core and 4.0 GB of system memory. Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, it relies on remote storage attachments. The instance achieves top-tier benchmark ratings in single-threaded compute workloads, notably across Geekbench single-core, stress-ng single-core, and gzip compression tasks, aided by modern AVX-512 and cryptographic extensions. However, its multi-core capabilities and total memory capacity remain limited by the dual-thread envelope, placing aggregate throughput in the lower percentiles. The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio delivers cost efficiency for operations requiring high-frequency single-thread execution without the overhead of surplus RAM. The server is well positioned for lightweight compute-bound services, CI/CD build agents, text processing scripts, and static web serving.
